sources.title: r/Python: Structure Large Python Projects for Maintainability
Modern Python Tooling in 2026 - uv, Ruff, ty

languages.name: Python
languages.notes: 3.13 is the safe, broadly-supported stable (bugfix through 2029, free-threaded mode experimental via PEP 703, basic JIT via PEP 744). 3.14.5 is the latest stable (released 2026-05-10). Prefer 3.13 for widest library/agent-tool compatibility; use 3.14 only after validating the full dependency stack.

libraries.name: fastapi
libraries.purpose: ASGI web framework for building typed APIs from Python type hints; auto OpenAPI docs, dependency injection, on par with Node/Go for I/O-bound APIs. Stands on Starlette + Pydantic.

libraries.name: django
libraries.purpose: Batteries-included full-stack framework (ORM, admin, auth, CSRF, templates). 6.1 adds async ORM field fetch modes; native async ORM methods aget/acreate/aupdate since 6.0.

libraries.name: flask
libraries.purpose: Minimal WSGI microframework for small services/JSON APIs. WSGI-only by design; async def views run in a worker thread via asgiref, not a real event loop.

libraries.name: pydantic
libraries.purpose: Type-hint-driven data validation and serialization (Rust-backed pydantic-core). Powers FastAPI, LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK, Pydantic AI. model_validate / model_dump API.

libraries.name: sqlalchemy
libraries.purpose: SQL toolkit and ORM with first-class async engine (create_async_engine, AsyncSession). Use with asyncpg for Postgres in async services.

libraries.name: pandas
libraries.purpose: Tabular data analysis/manipulation. 3.0 (Jan 2026) enforces Copy-on-Write, makes PyArrow string dtype default, requires Python 3.11+, adds zero-copy Arrow interchange.

libraries.name: numpy
libraries.purpose: N-dimensional arrays and vectorized math; the numerical backend for pandas, scikit-learn, PyTorch stacks. 2.x is a C-API-breaking modern baseline.

libraries.name: httpx
libraries.purpose: Modern HTTP client with sync Client + async AsyncClient, HTTP/2, default timeouts, full typing; the standard in-process test client for FastAPI/Starlette (calls ASGI apps directly).

libraries.name: aiohttp
libraries.purpose: Async HTTP client AND server built on asyncio; highest throughput for high-concurrency request storms. Pair with aiohttp-socks for SOCKS proxies.

libraries.name: requests
libraries.purpose: The classic synchronous/blocking HTTP client. Still ubiquitous for simple scripts; prefer httpx for new async or typed code.

libraries.name: pytest
libraries.purpose: Fixture-based test framework. 9.x removes 8.x deprecations, adds subtests, native [tool.pytest] TOML config. Pair with pytest-asyncio/anyio for async tests.

libraries.name: uv
libraries.purpose: Rust-powered single binary replacing pip/venv/poetry/pyenv; 10-100x faster. uv python install, uv init, uv add, uv sync, uv.lock cross-platform lockfile. Astral (acquired by OpenAI Mar 2026).

libraries.name: ruff
libraries.purpose: Single ultra-fast linter+formatter (replaces flake8/black/isort/pyupgrade/bandit-partial). Config in [tool.ruff]; `ruff check --fix`, `ruff format`.

libraries.name: typer
libraries.purpose: FastAPI's little sibling for CLIs: build terminal apps from type hints. Ideal for agent/automation entrypoints and ops tooling.

libraries.name: pydantic-ai
libraries.purpose: Type-safe agent framework from the Pydantic team (Apache 2.0). V1 API-stable since Sept 2025; structured outputs, tool calls, multi-model. Good for local-first agent automation.

patterns.title: Async I/O for concurrent HTTP calls
patterns.problem: Sequential blocking HTTP calls make I/O-bound agents/services slow and tie up the event loop.
patterns.solution: Use `async def` handlers and a single reused httpx.AsyncClient; gather concurrent calls with asyncio.gather.
patterns.anti_pattern: Creating a new client per request or calling sync requests.get inside an async handler (blocks the loop).
patterns.snippet:
async with httpx.AsyncClient() as c:
    res = await asyncio.gather(c.get(u) for u in urls)

patterns.title: Pydantic models for request/response contracts
patterns.problem: Untyped dicts let malformed input reach business logic and produce unclear 500s.
patterns.solution: Declare request bodies/responses as pydantic BaseModel and set response_model; FastAPI returns 422 on invalid input.
patterns.anti_pattern: Accepting raw dict and hand-validating with if/raise inside the route.

patterns.title: Dependency injection for shared resources
patterns.problem: Module-level global DB connections/auth state cause coupling and test friction.
patterns.solution: Provide resources via Depends(get_db) / Depends(get_current_user); FastAPI resolves the graph per request with caching.
patterns.anti_pattern: A module-global engine/session imported directly by handlers.

patterns.title: Dependency overrides for fast, isolated tests
patterns.problem: Tests hit the real database or external network, becoming slow and flaky.
patterns.solution: Override dependencies in tests: app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: fake_db; use ASGITransport for in-process HTTP.
patterns.anti_pattern: Importing and monkeypatching internals ad hoc, or running a real server on a port in unit tests.
patterns.snippet:
app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = lambda: fake_session
async with AsyncClient(transport=ASGITransport(app=app)) as c: ...

patterns.title: src/ layout with a separate tests/ folder
patterns.problem: Flat scripts and tests-inside-source cause circular imports, packaging bloat, and merge conflicts.
patterns.solution: Root-level src/<package>/ plus a sibling tests/ that mirrors the source structure (per Python Packaging User Guide).
patterns.anti_pattern: Scattering .py files at repo root or putting tests inside the importable package.

patterns.title: Gradual typing + CI type checking
patterns.problem: Untyped code ships runtime TypeErrors that tests miss and refactoring breaks silently.
patterns.solution: Annotate signatures/returns and run mypy/pyright/ty in CI; required by FastAPI models anyway.
patterns.anti_pattern: Spraying `Any` everywhere or disabling the type checker to silence errors.
patterns.snippet: # pyproject.toml [tool.pytest] + `uv run ty check` in CI

patterns.title: Reproducible environments with venv + lockfile
patterns.problem: Unpinned `pip install` causes dependency drift and 'works on my machine' failures.
patterns.solution: Isolate in a venv (or uv) and commit a lockfile (uv.lock / poetry.lock) with exact resolved versions.
patterns.anti_pattern: Installing packages globally or committing only unpinned requirements.txt.
patterns.snippet: uv sync   # installs exact versions from uv.lock

patterns.title: Context managers for resource safety
patterns.problem: Manually opened files/sessions/connections leak handles and locks.
patterns.solution: Use `with`/`async with` for files, sessions, and clients so cleanup is guaranteed.
patterns.anti_pattern: file = open(...) then forgetting close(), or relying on GC.
patterns.snippet:
async with AsyncSession(engine) as s:
    rows = await s.execute(select(User))

patterns.title: Pandas Copy-on-Write / explicit copies
patterns.problem: Chained assignment on a view silently mutates the parent DataFrame in surprising places.
patterns.solution: On pandas 3.0 CoW is default (subset mutations get a lazy copy). For older versions set mode.copy_on_write=True and use .copy() explicitly.
patterns.anti_pattern: df[mask]['col'] = val  (chained assignment on a possibly-view).
patterns.snippet: subset = df.iloc[1:3].copy()  # own the data before mutating

patterns.title: pytest fixtures over duplicated setup
patterns.problem: Each test repeats setup/teardown, drifting and hiding intent.
patterns.solution: Declare fixtures (client, db_session, auth) with scope and yield; depend on them by argument.
patterns.anti_pattern: Copy-pasting connect/insert/cleanup boilerplate into every test function.

methodologies.name: Test-Driven Development (TDD)
methodologies.summary: Write a failing test before the implementation, then make it pass and refactor; keeps behavior pinned and designs testable code.
methodologies.steps:
1. Write a small failing test for the next behavior
2. Run it to confirm it fails for the right reason
3. Write the minimal code to make it pass
4. Refactor while green
5. Repeat; keep the suite in CI with a coverage gate

methodologies.name: Gradual / Type-Driven Development
methodologies.summary: Annotate code and let a type checker (mypy/pyright/ty) act as a compile-time safety net; especially effective with Pydantic and FastAPI.
methodologies.steps:
1. Add type hints to new functions first
2. Run the type checker in CI on every PR
3. Enable strict mode incrementally
4. Fix errors before merge; never blanket-ignore
5. Use pydantic models as the data boundary

methodologies.name: 12-Factor App for Python Services
methodologies.summary: Build stateless, config-outside-code services: env-based config, explicit deps, logs to stdout, one codebase per app.
methodologies.steps:
1. One codebase, tracked in git
2. Declare and pin dependencies (uv.lock)
3. Store config in environment, not code
4. Treat backing services (DB, cache) as attached resources
5. Ship logs to stdout; run as stateless processes

methodologies.name: CI/CD with GitHub Actions
methodologies.summary: Automate lint + type-check + test + build on every push so regressions are caught before merge.
methodologies.steps:
1. On push/PR: uv sync
2. ruff check --fix && ruff format --check
3. ty check (or mypy)
4. uv run pytest with coverage threshold
5. Build wheel/container on main; deploy from tag

methodologies.name: Reproducible Dependency Management
methodologies.summary: Lockfiles and isolated environments make builds deterministic across machines and CI.
methodologies.steps:
1. Create an isolated env (uv venv / python -m venv)
2. Add deps via uv add (writes uv.lock)
3. Commit the lockfile
4. Install in CI with uv sync --frozen
5. Refresh deliberately (uv lock --upgrade) and re-test

methodologies.name: Dependency Injection / Clean Architecture
methodologies.summary: Pass dependencies (DB, config, clients) into functions/handlers instead of importing globals; improves testability and decoupling.
methodologies.steps:
1. Define provider functions (get_db, get_settings)
2. Inject via FastAPI Depends or constructor args
3. Override providers in tests
4. Keep business logic free of framework imports
5. Separate domain, service, and transport layers
